subject: Fraud & Scams
title: What Identity Theft Really Means
description: A quick, practical guide to What Identity Theft Really Means.

hook.text: Someone opens a credit card in your name, maxes it out, and vanishes. You get the bill.

buildup.text: Identity theft means someone uses your personal information to commit fraud or theft.

discovery.text: It can take months or years for victims to discover the crime and repair the damage.

twist.text: Victims often spend more time fighting the aftermath than the thief spent committing the crime.

climax.text: Identity theft is now the fastest-growing crime in the world, affecting millions each year.

punchline.text: Your identity is valuable. Thieves know it better than you.

quiz.question: What makes identity theft particularly damaging to victims?
options: It can take months or years to discover and repair
